references.text: Jesus' use of the term 'Son of God' in his defense against the blasphemy charge is a direct reference to Psalm 82:6, where he argues that if those who received God's word could be called 'gods,' how much more so he whom the Father set apart and sent into the world.

The title 'Son of God' that Jesus uses to defend himself against the charge of blasphemy has its theological root in Psalm 2:7, where the Messiah is declared as God's own Son, underscoring the unique relationship Jesus has with the Father.
The same accusation of blasphemy arises earlier in the Gospel of John when Jesus calls God his own Father, showing a recurring conflict over his identity as the Son of God and equality with God.
The Jews' charge of blasphemy against Jesus because he claimed to be the Son of God is repeated at the crucifixion, where they maintain that he deserves death for making himself the Son of God.
